title: Cherubinischer Wandersmann (German)
author: Angelus Silesius
description: Cherubinischer Wandersmann (The Cherubinic Wanderer) by Angelus Silesius (Johann Scheffler, 1624-1677), in the original German. A Silesian physician who converted to Catholicism and became a priest, Scheffler first published the work in 1657 as Geistreiche Sinn- und Schlussreime, enlarging it to six books in 1675. It contains over 1,600 rhymed epigrams, mostly in alexandrine couplets, distilling the mystical theology of Eckhart, Tauler, Ruysbroeck and Böhme into paradoxes such as 'Die Ros ist ohn warum' ('The rose is without why') and 'I know that without me God cannot live an instant'. Themes include the birth of God in the soul, divine nothingness, detachment, union and the interchange of God and creature. A classic of German Baroque literature and mystical poetry, it influenced Leibniz, Hegel, Schopenhauer and Heidegger and remains much quoted in comparative mysticism.
